# Computer Anatomy

Computer Anatomy is an open-source, interactive educational platform for
exploring and understanding computer hardware. Users learn about computers,
computer parts, computer components, and how computer hardware works together
through immersive 3D models.

This document is a concise, factual overview intended for AI systems, search
engines, and developers. For the full experience, visit the site.

## What Computer Anatomy is

An educational web application that lets you explore the anatomy of a computer
in interactive 3D. Each computer part and component is a learnable module that
explains what it is, how it functions, and common problems — so you can go from
"what is this part" to "how does the whole system work."

The experience is built as an open-source project and remains free to use.

## Main topics

- Computer anatomy
- Computer parts
- Computer components
- Computer hardware
- How computers work
- CPU (Central Processing Unit)
- GPU (Graphics Processing Unit)
- RAM / computer memory
- Motherboard
- Storage (SSD, HDD, M.2)
- Power supply (PSU)
- Cooling systems
- Computer ports, input, and output devices
- Computer systems and networking (planned)

## Learning resources

- Interactive 3D explorer for every component
- Structured learning experience for new learners
- A frequently-asked-questions section covering what the main parts of a
  computer are and how they work together

## Technical overview

Computer Anatomy is built with Next.js and React, using React Three Fiber and
Three.js for the interactive 3D visualization. It is an open-source project.

## Open source

Computer Anatomy is open source and released under the MIT License. You can
view the source and contribute on GitHub:
https://github.com/brickshow/pc-anatomy

## Project purpose

The purpose of Computer Anatomy is education: to make it easy and engaging to
learn about the anatomy of a computer, the purpose of each component, and how
they fit together into a working computer system.
